keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 413,744 km2 (the Natural Earth country; the page gives no area): the republic of October 1924, whose borders "remained unchanged" through 1991. Cliopatria has no row; the land lies inside its Union of Soviet Socialist Republics shapes and begins as Turkmenistan in 1992. The part of Shirabad the page adds from the Bukharan republic is not placed.

ledger.note: 1924, October: the Politburo divided the territories "In October 1924" and the lands "were unified to create the Turkmen Soviet Socialist Republic"; the core is the Transcaspian Oblast of the Turkestan ASSR.

region.text: Chardzhou (Charjew) and Kerki on the Amu Darya, from Bukhara

ledger.note: 1924, October: Charjew, Kerki and part of Shirabad join from the Bukharan People's Republic.
1924, October: "the Turkmen (Dasoguz) province of Khorezm People's Republic" joins.
1925, 13 May: a separate republic of the USSR "as the Turkmen SSR".
1991, 27 October: "it became independent as Turkmenistan" (sovereignty declared 22 August 1990; recognised 26 December 1991).

certainty.note: "The borders of Soviet Turkmenistan remained unchanged."

sources.title: Turkmen Soviet Socialist Republic
sources.note: October 1924 created; 13 May 1925 separate USSR republic; borders unchanged; sovereignty 22 August 1990; 27 October 1991; capital Ashgabat; no area.

notes: No Cliopatria row; the land lies inside Union of Soviet Socialist Republics shapes (1924-1991); Cliopatria's Turkmenistan begins in 1992. The republic is an internal unit of the Soviet Union. The page gives the month only ("In October 1924"); the Bukharan and Khorezm dossiers date the abolition to October 1924. The page is silent on the area, on Uzbek border changes and on the name Poltoratsk for Ashgabat. The part of Shirabad is not placed. Counterparts turkestan-assr, bukharan-people-s-soviet-republic and khorezm-people-s-soviet-republic have dossiers.
